MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 7, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:04 p.m., on July 7, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 2, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Liability Claim Pursuant to California Government
  Code Section 54956.95. Claimant: Michelle Miranda; Agency Claimed Against: City
  of Mission Viejo; Insurance Pool; Workman’s Compensation.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: 2 potential cases.

City Council Minutes  1  July 7, 2014
 CS3. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council began with a special meeting at 4:00
p.m., covering the same closed session agenda matters. During the 4:00 session, the Council
received information on item CS1 and gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

At 5:00 p.m., the City Council continued the closed session and considered the first of two
matters for item CS2. The Council received an update and gave direction to staff but no
reportable action occurred. Mr. Curley announced that the City Council will return to closed
session, after the end of the regular meeting tonight, to deal with the second matter for item CS2
and to address item CS3.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Employees and Customer of Leslie’s Pool Supply for Their Life Saving
  Efforts

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of appreciation to Ron Eroh, James Doherty, and Mark
  Dorey for rendering aid and helping to save the life of Craig Chandler.

P2. Proclaim July 2014 as Recreation & Parks Month

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Mark Nix and recreation department staff.

P3. Recognize Terry Wedel of KSBR Radio on his Retirement

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Terry Wedel.

P4. Presentation by the Orange County Vector Control District on the Public Health
  Alert: The Asian Tiger Mosquito

City Council Minutes  2  July 7, 2014
   The City Council received the presentation from Jared Dever, Orange County Vector
  Control District.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

David Anderson, representing Saddleback College, M.V.: invited the community to the
Saddleback College campus for a professional musical theater presentation of Godspell on
August 1 and 2, 2014, and he extended a special invitation to the City Council for the Friday
night performance. Mr. Anderson noted that this is a free, family-friendly event with great
preshow activities and residents can either bring a picnic or purchase food that evening.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: referencing closed session item CS3, she stated that she hopes the City
Manager does not receive a raise because the City employees have not. Mrs. Reavis referred to
an article in the local paper on public employee benefits and she discussed the City's own
CalPERS benefits and expenses. Lastly, Mrs. Reavis announced that she is not in favor of shade
structures at the tennis center because she feels they should be erected at facilities that everyone
can use, not just at private facilities.

Chuck Robinson, M.V.: stated that there are a lot of good cities in Orange County but Mission
Viejo is a great one. He noted that Mission Viejo has the best facilities, including the library and
community center, the recreation centers and 53 parks; the best events and programs; the best
residents and volunteers; and a City Council that sets policy and budget and staff who take the
steps to follow through.

Donna Lang Stoffel, M.V.: announced that Mission Viejo Boy Scout Troop 787 is celebrating its
40th anniversary and she invited the Council Members to attend a celebration on Saturday July
12, 2014, from 12:00 to 5:00 p.m. at Coast Bible Church. She noted that Troop 787 was one of
the first troops in Mission Viejo and in South County and is one of the most recognized troops in
all of Orange County.

Ron Simpson, Lake Forest: discussing agenda item 32, he made a distinction between group
homes (also known as halfway housed) and residential care homes for the elderly. He stated that
residential care homes are pretty special and make a significant difference in the quality of life
for the elderly.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo offers programs for small children all the way
up to the senior population. There is something for everyone whether in the parks or at City
facilities and she thanked this City Council and prior Councils for making parks and recreation a
priority. She also thanked the volunteers who made the 4th of July Street Faire another great
event, she discussed the recent Nadadores Swim Meet of Champions which had 2,000 attendees
a day, and she announced that her husband, Paul Bucknum, is the new President of the Mission
Viejo Rotary Club.

City Council Minutes  3  July 7, 2014
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 13, 17, 18, 19, and 22 were removed from the Consent Calendar for
separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 16, 2014, as presented.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget - Fiscal Year 2014-15

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 14-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority (MVHA) for FY 2014-15.

10. Renewal of Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order for year 2 of 5 year agreement in the amount of
  $57,205.42 for maintenance and support of the Library Automated System (ALS) Software
  and Hardware Agreement with SirsiDynix, Inc.

  Approved issuance of a purchase order to CompuCom, Inc. for such services for 2014-15 in
  the amount of $74,968.94.

12. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Agreement

  Approved 3-year agreement and issuance of purchase orders to Digital Map Products, Inc.

14. Transfer of Southern California Edison Rule 20A Allocations
City Council Minutes  4  July 7, 2014
   Authorized the City Manager to enter into an agreement with the City of Newport Beach to
  transfer the City's unused Rule 20A allocation of $99,143.00 within the Southern California
  Edison (SCE) Service Area to the City of Newport Beach in exchange for compensation in

15. 2014 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)-Slurry Seal

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

16. Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 Freeway to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)

  (1) Approved the Reimbursement Agreement with Moulton Niguel Water District subject
  to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney and/or City Engineer; and (2)
  approved the Reimbursement Agreement with Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development

20. Request by the Cultural Arts Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City of Mission Viejo Civic Center,
  Saddleback Room. Event - Photography Exhibit Reception and Concert on Sunday,
  September 14, 2014 at 1:00 pm.

  Approved the request of the Cultural Arts Committee for a one-time exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation for the Photography Exhibit Reception and
  Concert in the Civic Center, Saddleback Room.

21. Request for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  regulation at City Facilities for the Anniversary Celebration featuring the Pacific
  Symphony Orchestra.

  Approved the onetime exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation
  for the "Symphony in the Cities" featuring the Pacific Symphony Orchestra on Saturday,
  July 26, 2014 on the "Village Green" in Oso Viejo Community Park.

23. Measure M2 Environmental Clean-Up Program Applications for Marguerite
  Parkway Medians

  Adopted Resolution 14-35 Authorizing Staff to Apply for Funds for the Environmental
  Cleanup, Tier 1 Grant Program under Orange County Local Transportation Ordinance No.
  3 for the Marguerite Parkway Roadway Pollutant and Runoff Abatement Projects.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  5  July 7, 2014
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Reardon

34. Electronic Cigarettes: Preliminary Research on the Myths vs. the Facts

  Ashlyn Olson, Intern for Council Member Reardon, presented information on e-cigarettes
  and answered the City Council Members questions based on her research.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

19. Proposed Lease Agreement Submitted by Verizon Wireless in Conjunction with
  Proposal to Construct a Wireless Telecommunications Facility at Gilleran Park,
  24960 Felipe Road, on Property Owned by the City of Mission Viejo

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern about wireless telecommunication facilities
  and stated that she believes there are issues with the EMF being over the legal limit at some
  sites. She noted that Planning and Transportation Commissioner Bill Ernisse has seen the
  readings on at least two sites and she feels the cell companies have not done the self-
  monitoring that their contract with the City requires. Council Member Schlicht stated that
  there are public health risks and she asked the City Attorney if the City can place a
  moratorium on new facilities until we get the radio frequency (RF) readings in alignment
  with the Federal guidelines.

  City Attorney Bill Curley responded that the City could institute a moratorium however the
  cell companies could seek a Federal review to trump that. He noted that this is the first he
  has heard that they are not following the RF guidelines and he suggested that the City ask
  the cell companies for demonstration of compliance instead of establishing a moratorium.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister responded to the question about EMF
  measurements and stated that residents and a commissioner got readings that were higher
  than the FCC recommends, however she noted that taking the readings can be complex.
  Mrs. Lister said that staff will be discussing the matter further however nothing has been
  concluded at this point. She also mentioned that the site being considered this evening is
  not up and running yet so it cannot be out of compliance.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve
  and authorize the City Manager to Execute the Lease (A14-30).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  July 7, 2014
 22. Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she does not believe in lobbyists and feels that they
  are hired guns. She noted that if the Council wishes to retain a lobbyist, it is time to go out
  for competitive bid.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve
  the Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs for State legislative
  advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed the amount of $60,000
  for the period of July 1, 2014, to June 30, 2015.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

Council Member Schlicht

36. Was the Sierra Playground Survey Rigged?

  Council Member Schlicht presented the report and stated that she feels that polling
  residents in the surrounding neighborhood was discriminatory and equivalent to stuffing the
  ballot box. She feels that only the recreation center members’ opinions should be
  considered when addressing agenda item 24.

OLD BUSINESS

24. Sierra Recreation Center Play Area (CIP 323)

  Mayor Kelley announced that she has a recommendation that might make many people
  happy and that is to move the playground from the currently projected location to the other
  side of the pool.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Andrew Blenkle, M.V.: expressed opposition to the proposed play structure and stated that
  the people he knows do not want a playground at Sierra.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1) reject all
  bids for the Sierra Recreation Center playground installation for the proposed location; (2)
  direct City staff to redesign the proposed playground equipment layout into the north grass
  area of the Sierra Recreation Center; and (3) authorize staff to re-bid both the current layout

City Council Minutes  7  July 7, 2014
   and the new layout of the playground and return to the City Council as soon as possible
  with a bid for each location for Council review and consideration.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

25. Possible Renaming of Alicia Park to William S. Craycraft Park

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: stated that the Community Services Commission and the committee
  that looked into this matter felt that Alicia Park was the most fitting site for naming
  after William (Bill) Craycraft and he noted that Bill's sons agreed.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon,
  approve the Community Services Commission’s recommendation for the renaming of
  Alicia Park to William S. Craycraft Park and adopt Resolution 14-36 to Appropriate $6,000
  Into the Parks Maintenance Program Budget in the General Fund From Unappropriated
  General Fund Reserves for Park Signage.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

32. Pacific Shores Properties LLC etc, et al v. City of Newport Beach: Consider
  Legislative Support and Optional Funding Contribution in Support of City Council’s
  Legislative Freedom

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  8  July 7, 2014
   The following spoke in favor of supporting the City of Newport Beach and for funding the
  legislation: Tricia Bramwell, M.V.; Jan Howard, M.V.; and John Kirsten, M.V.

  The following presented a written comment in favor of regulating board and care facilities:
  Cecil Sutherland, M.V.; Rick Barrett, M.V.; and Todd Bramwell, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 14-37 Expressing Support for the City of Newport Beach's Petition for U.S.
  Supreme Court Review of the Ninth Circuit's Decision in Pacific Shores, LLC et al., v. City
  of Newport Beach.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Leckness
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to provide
  $10,000 in funding contribution to assist in preserving the City Council of Mission Viejo's
  legislative discretion as regards to developing local legislation.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

18. City of Mission Viejo Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program (FY
  2014-15-FY 2020-21)

  Council Member Schlicht asked why the Council no longer gets copies of the Pavement
  Management Program at Council Meetings and she expressed her objection to the Cabot
  Road project which, she feels, benefits the City of Laguna Niguel more than Mission Viejo
  residents.

  Consultant Gail Shiomoto-Lohr stated that there is no longer a requirement, through the
  Measure M extension, to have the Council approve the Pavement Management Program
  therefore they are not placed on an agenda. She also noted that the Cabot Road project
  remains in an unfunded state however staff left it in as a placeholder and will continue to
  look for any funding opportunities that might become available. Ms. Shiomoto-Lohr agreed
  to provide the Council Members with a copy of the 2014 Pavement Management Program.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 14-34 Adopting a Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program
City Council Minutes  9  July 7, 2014
   Beginning with the 2014-2015 Fiscal Year; and (2) direct the Director of Public Works to
  transmit the adopted Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program to the
  Orange County Transportation Authority by July 31, 2014.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that Council Member Schlicht brought up two good questions
on solar lighting at the last City Council Meeting and he posed questions about the feasibility of
using solar lighting on Muirlands Boulevard.

31. Project Status Update on the Replacement and Implementation of the City’s Financial
  Management Software System.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander presented the staff report.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

3.  Check Register Dated June 6, 2014 in the Amount of $370,519.90

  Due to the late hour, this item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

4.  Check Register Dated June 13, 2014 in the Amount of $1,081,553.96

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

5.  Check Register dated June 20, 2014 in the amount of $603,024.16

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

6.  Adoption of FY 2014-15 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked questions about the CDA finances, interest and bonds and
  Director Dyas provided responses.

City Council Minutes  10  July 7, 2014
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  CDFA Resolution 14-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2014-15 Fiscal Year.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

13. Public Works Professional Services Consultant Team

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

17. 2014 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)-CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she pulled this item so she can register a no
  vote. She stated that All American Asphalt did a poor job on Olympiad Road between
  Alicia and Jeronimo and it remains a driving hazard for motorcycles.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  award the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt in the
  amount of $2,027,027.00, and (2) adopt Resolution No. 14-33 Amending the Fiscal Year

City Council Minutes  11  July 7, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Reardon

  Council Member Reardon returned to the dais at 9:26 p.m.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION,COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

26. Community Services Commission Vacancy

  Council Member Reardon nominated Ellen Natsume to serve as a senior member on the
  Community Services Commission. The nomination was ratified by consensus of the City
  Council.

27. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that for over a year he has been warning the City that the
  reserves are in jeopardy and there is now proposed legislation that would enforce that a city
  withdrawing from the OCFA would still be liable for a portion of the unfunded liability.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

28. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCTA

29. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness announced that the Vector Control District update was
  presented earlier in the evening during agenda item P4.

30. SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg informed the City Council that an SDG&E contractor hit an electrical line
while working on the Oso Parkway widening project. Electricity was out for a period of time
last night, all day today and tonight the crews will continue working to repair the line. He noted
that the Oso Parkway #3 westbound lane will be closed again during the morning commute.
City Council Minutes  12  July 7, 2014
 City Attorney’s Report

Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney about the whistleblower hotline.

City Attorney Curley responded that the phone line has been ordered and it should be activated
this week.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

33. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon stated that she had planned to show a video teaser for the new MVTV
four-part prescription drug abuse program however due to the late hour, she will delay the video
until August.

Council Member Schlicht

35. Special Fire Protection Area (SFPA) Overview

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Council Member Reardon read a prepared statement regarding the SFPA and announced
  that she will be giving the City Clerk some of the documentation for the public record.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she did not come forward with her information on the
  SFPA without having some background. She said that the SFPA was developed to avoid
  disclosure and she feels the Council received poor legal advice. She recommended that
  homeowners disclose the location of their homes to insurance companies or potential
  buyers and that they check with an attorney for legal advice.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury noted that it is important that the Council transmits information to the
residents that they can actually digest. He stated that the last hour of this meeting was difficult
for anyone to follow.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that he too had a video he wanted to show this evening but
given the late hour, he decided not to share it. Instead he encouraged residents to watch the new
MVTV program with a resident touring the Olympic bicycle course in Mission Viejo. Mayor
City Council Minutes  13  July 7, 2014
 Pro Tem Leckness shared an idea with his colleagues that the City host a walk around Lake
Mission Viejo for wheelchair-bound individuals. He noted that it would send a message that we
are interested in outdoor activities for all residents, not just for athletes.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley introduced the City’s new Orange County Register reporter, Tomoya
Shimura. She announced that the 4th of July Street Fair was a tremendous success and she
thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee volunteers. Mayor Kelley encouraged anyone
interested in joining the Activities Committee to contact her for more information. She also
reminded residents that Pacific Symphony will play at Oso Viejo Park on July 26 and there will
be a small ceremony to commemorate the 30th anniversary of the Olympics on July 29. The
event will be held at the finish line on Olympiad and will feature the unveiling of an Olympic
rings monument. Mayor Kelley announced that the City Council will be dark from now until
August 18 unless the need arises for a special meeting.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 1:13 a.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, August 18, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.
